nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$, $n$ and $p$, $p$ is the $k$-th smallest prime factor of $n$ when $n \ne 0$, $p$ is a prime dividing $n$, and exactly $k - 1$ primes dividing $n$ are smaller than $p$.
nodes.title: The $k$-th smallest prime factor

nodes.summary: A function $f \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ is unimodal on the primes if there is a prime $p_0$ such that $f(p) \le f(q)$ for all primes $p$ and $q$ with $p \le q \le p_0$, and $f(q) \le f(p)$ for all primes $p$ and $q$ with $p_0 \le p \le q$.
nodes.title: Unimodality on the primes

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $p$, let $S_{k,p}$ be the set of natural numbers whose $k$-th smallest prime factor is $p$. The $k$-th prime-factor density $d_k(p)$ is the natural density of $S_{k,p}$, that is, the limit of $\lvert S_{k,p} \cap \{0, 1, \dots, N - 1\} \rvert / N$ as $N \to \infty$, when this limit exists; otherwise $d_k(p)$ is an unspecified real number.
